_about: Who uses each file in <data>/secrets, what it is (about), how to get or replace it (how), and what the host watcher does when it changes (apply). Read by the hub (Secrets screen) and the watcher. A key under companions/{companion}/ matches that file in every companion's own secrets folder (cluster.json companions), and {companion} in apply values is that companion's name. apply: copy = install the file at that path for the agent; restart = restart the container whose name starts with it.

cloudflare-api.token.label: Cloudflare API token
cloudflare-api.token.note: Read each time agentctl talks to Cloudflare.
cloudflare-api.token.about: A Cloudflare API token that lets agentctl create the tunnel, its DNS records and the Access application and policy that sign people in.
cloudflare-api.token.how: Cloudflare dashboard → My Profile → API Tokens → Create token, with Account · Cloudflare Tunnel: Edit, Account · Access: Apps and Policies: Edit, and Zone · DNS: Edit for the zone. Then run `agentctl cloudflare setup`.

cloudflare-tunnel.token.label: Cloudflare Tunnel token
cloudflare-tunnel.token.note: Read when cloudflared starts: run `agentctl apply` (or restart cloudflared) after changing it.
cloudflare-tunnel.token.about: The token cloudflared on the server uses to connect the tunnel. Everything people open goes through it; nothing on the server listens publicly.
cloudflare-tunnel.token.how: Written by `agentctl cloudflare setup`. To rotate: Zero Trust → Networks → Tunnels → the tunnel → refresh token, paste it here, then run `agentctl apply`.

coolify.token.label: Coolify API token
coolify.token.note: Read each time a deploy runs.
coolify.token.about: An API token of the Coolify instance that runs every stack. agentctl and the Configs screen push the rendered compose files and trigger deploys with it.
coolify.token.how: Coolify → Keys & Tokens → API tokens → create one with deploy permissions; paste it here and delete the old one.

companions/{companion}/bot-token.txt.label: Companion · Slack bot token
companions/{companion}/bot-token.txt.about: The Bot User OAuth token (starts with xoxb-) of the companion's Slack app. The companion posts, reads threads and uploads files with it.
companions/{companion}/bot-token.txt.how: api.slack.com/apps → the app → OAuth & Permissions → Bot User OAuth Token. Reinstalling the app to the workspace issues a new one.

companions/{companion}/app-token.txt.label: Companion · Slack app token (socket mode)
companions/{companion}/app-token.txt.about: The app-level token (starts with xapp-) with connections:write. The companion opens its Socket Mode connection to Slack with it, so nothing on the server is exposed.
companions/{companion}/app-token.txt.how: api.slack.com/apps → the app → Basic Information → App-Level Tokens → generate one with the connections:write scope (revoke the old one).

companions/{companion}/user-token.txt.label: Companion · Slack user token (reads as the owner)
companions/{companion}/user-token.txt.about: The owner's own User OAuth token (starts with xoxp-), read-only scopes. It lets the companion see messages that mention or DM the owner. It cannot post as them.
companions/{companion}/user-token.txt.how: api.slack.com/apps → the app → OAuth & Permissions → User OAuth Token (appears after installing the app with user scopes). Reinstall to rotate.

companions/{companion}/owner.txt.label: Companion · owner's Slack member id
companions/{companion}/owner.txt.about: Not really a secret: the Slack member id of the person the companion works for. It only takes orders, approvals and Send taps from them.
companions/{companion}/owner.txt.how: In Slack: the profile → ⋯ → Copy member ID (looks like U0…).

companions/{companion}/agent-key.txt.label: Companion ↔ agent bridge key
companions/{companion}/agent-key.txt.about: A random shared password. The agent's Accounts app only accepts the companion's calls (start a T3 chat, send a message, answer a question, stop a run) when they carry this key.
companions/{companion}/agent-key.txt.how: Any long random string, e.g. the output of `openssl rand -hex 32`. Saving it here installs it in the agent too, then restarts the companion.

companions/{companion}/github-app-id.txt.label: Companion · GitHub App ID
companions/{companion}/github-app-id.txt.about: The numeric App ID of the companion's GitHub App. With the private key below, the companion lists the open pull requests of every repo the App is installed on and posts reviews and QA reports as its bot. Empty means reviews are off.
companions/{companion}/github-app-id.txt.how: GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → GitHub Apps → the App → General → App ID.

companions/{companion}/github-app-key.pe.label: Companion · GitHub App private key
companions/{companion}/github-app-key.pe.about: The App's private key (a .pem file). The companion mints short-lived installation tokens with it; whatever the App is installed on is what it can review. It never leaves the companion.
companions/{companion}/github-app-key.pe.how: The App's page → General → Private keys → Generate a private key; paste the whole .pem here, then delete any older key on GitHub.

companions/{companion}/work-tools.md.label: Companion · work tools (optional)
companions/{companion}/work-tools.md.about: Optional notes for the companion: which tools and accounts it may use for errands. Plain text it reads at start.
companions/{companion}/work-tools.md.how: Write it here in plain words; the companion restarts with it.
